The exact odd-degree covector theorem, rank formula and generic-stratum full-image theorem are proved. Whenever an etale polarized odd isogeny B->A of multipliern has an integral nodal individual theta image, full GL_(m²-1) for \|mTheta_B\|, m=3e odd, transfers to full GL_(n²m²-1) for \|mnTheta_A\|. This arbitrary-odd good-theta transfer is now complete: the finite four-value exceptional set gives2-transitivity; isolated theta-boundary collisions give supported transpositions and the full node permutation product; actual natural blocks, normal Lang extension, all kernel shifts and transvection generation give the full group. No full stable-fibre identification across a rank drop is assumed. Every fixed f0 genus-two Jacobian has proved nodal5- and7-self-isogenies on the SAME surface. Combining them with the known3-power family gives, for all i,j,k>=0 and d=3^i5^j7^k, geometric and arithmetic group GL_(9d²-1). For d=a+b with botha,b of that form, the group is F2^(9d²-4) semidirect GL_(9d²-4), in rank9d²-3. The earlier exact bounded family census included every even degree2 through90. The later nine-theta transfer now closes every remaining f0 even degree; the then-remaining f0 odd degree11 is now closed by the later norm-eleven theorem. For each fixed f1 principal surface the proved odd degrees are3^i, and the proved even degrees are3^i+3^j. The even group is Hom(F2²,F2^(9d²-4)) semidirect GL_(9d²-4), in rank9d²-2. The smallest remaining f1 degrees are5 and8. A suitable incoming nodal5-neighbour for every such fixed surface remains unproved. Every fixed supersingular or mixed elliptic product has the corresponding exact odd/even groups in every balanced degree, and the prior mixed-strip results remain proved. In each even group the common covector kernel is irreducible and contained in every nonzero invariant subspace. Geometrically generic nonordinary ppav strata are classified in every degree, and any finite prescribed degree set has a common nonempty open and finite-field examples. The explicit F16 five-kernel census and its20 nodal self-isogeny kernels remain separately verified. Arbitrary fixed nonproduct degrees outside the families above and the structural classification for generalX stay open. The universal norm7 quaternion interpolation now has its complete triple-fibre exclusion. It treats infinity, Z=0, conjugate points and both A(L) branches before the exact resultant calculation. The degree97 bad-r radical and its cubic-remainder gcd z³+z²+1 let one choose a good presentation of every fixed modulus. The resulting theta image has exactly48 nodes. This is a universal proof with exact identities, not an extrapolation from the retained finite-parameter explorations. For f<=1 and any odd kernel, a tangency forces a three-point fibre through a Weierstrass representative of geometric2-torsion. Thus excluding three-point fibres suffices for nodality; existence of the incoming isogeny is still required. This explicit counterexample does not settle the required existence of a good incoming neighbour and closes no remaining degree. The complete nine-theta transfer works through ANY odd polarized isogeny with indecomposable nonordinary source, without principal-theta nodality. Three movable cubic components give clean isolated contacts; their162-node type permutations and exact eighteen-label graph lifts force every translation heart. These geometric and arithmetic groups are exact. Remaining odd fixed-f0 degrees and the fixed-f1 degree5 gate remain open; no all-degree conclusion is made. In f1, the unique ordinary and supersingular elliptic subvarieties have the same principal degree d; a product prime-ell quotient forces d=ell and the unique possible kernelEo[ell]=Es[ell]. They do not change the exact-group cases already established. The rank for an arbitrary functional and larger point configurations remains unresolved. Symmetry-normalized theta translations identify the parameter with the squared cubic-theta embedding at a fixed geometric2-torsion shift. The embedding excludes singularity for every twist not killed by2. Outgoing odd-isogeny character decomposition therefore gives maximal dual alternating rank9d^2-1 for every fixed nonordinary principal surface in every odd\|3dTheta\|. This is distinct from the previously proved generic curve p-rank. The incidence, local inertia and global generation steps connecting this dual rank to new full monodromy cases remain open; no additional exact-group degree is claimed solely from this result. The subsequent common-incidence proof closes the gap between separate generic ranks: the other contraction is literally the same Moore pencil, and the degree-one symmetrizer identifies the actual trivial left kernel linearly with the same section variable. All multiplication and dual determinant opens meet, with bijective relative Frobenius on a smooth connected pullback curve. Consequently the actual left-kernel map is separably dominant and birational in every fixed odd principal-cube degree. The remaining local gate is a nonempty corank-one Hasse wall inside this common open, followed by global full-radical generation; no new exact-group degree is asserted from birationality alone. The conditional wall theorem now proves that any nonempty Hasse wall inside the common maximal-rank open is smooth with simple determinant order, stable loss exactlyone, and full hyperplane-radical inertia. Maximal kernel variation excludes a further nilpotent step. Nonemptiness of that wall and the required global generation remain unproved; separate nonzero ambient determinants do not prove nonvanishing on the degree-one Hasse cubic. |

The lower examples are actual Barsotti-Tate groups over explicitly defined complete DVR fields, not merely coefficient profiles. The construction actually works whenever p(p-1) divides e and e>p^2; no least-index formula for every such e is claimed. ALL VALUATION-ONE IRREDUCIBLE RESIDUAL COMPARISONS: at every e=t p(p-1), p not dividing t, an actual p^3 isomorphism between whole potentially supersingular height-two groups with irreducible residual inertia determines the requested special characters. Exact point-field ramification, both cyclotomic tower cases and the selected actual critical coefficients are all treated. Reducible branches and mixed groups at arbitrary e remain separate. Earlier exact cases and remaining general gate: CURRENT EXACT FIRST-WILD CONCLUSION: nu_min(5,20,2)=2 in the full B.4 height-two setting. Actual125-torsion determines every requested prime-to-five finite special character, and the explicit B63 whole-versus-filtered construction gives actual25-torsion ambiguity. The completed maximal unramified base has the same absolute index and inertia question, and contains mu5 by the explicit tame/Cohen/Hensel argument. No residual pattern at p5,e20 remains open. WIDER FIRST-WILD RESULT: for every p>=5 at e=p(p-1), an actual p^3 comparison of whole potentially supersingular height-two groups with irreducible residual inertia determines the special characters. B97 proves exact actual point-field degrees p^2 and point conductors c1=(p^2-1)(p-1), c2=(p^4-1)(p-1), and bounds every terminal character by p^(r1-2)c2. Traceless first layers are excluded. In the traceful case, the actual two-tower different estimate gives delta1+p*delta2>=p(p^2-p-1); the first cyclotomic quotient bounds delta1<=p-1, so the last restricted cyclotomic character exceeds the terminal bound. The common first cyclotomic layer is explicitly retained. No CM or abelian-image hypothesis is imposed. For p>=7 the reducible-residual branches are not closed by this theorem; the unrestricted first-wild least index there remains in{2,3}. OTHER EXACT CASES: height1 has least index0. For p not dividing e, B74 gives nu_min<=n-1 when e<p^n,n>=3; B75 improves the full filtered bound for n>=4 to e<p^(n-1)(p+1). The n3 formal improvement is not asserted as a full index2 theorem. Dimensions are detected for n>=v_p(e)+2. REMAINING GATE: determine the reducible first-wild branches at primes>=7, wild absolute indices outside the newly closed e=2p(p-1) family, the remaining larger tame exact intervals (including p5,e752), and the general higher-height function. The smallest remaining first-wild prime is7 in that named family; no claim that it is the globally smallest open B.4 parameter is made. Earlier necessary p5/e20 images and parameters are proof history, now all excluded; their exact proofs and former gates remain in the preceding immutable checkpoints and dated ledger. |

## Corrections and audit cautions

1. A.1: the prompt says there is no section 8.2. Both supplied witnesses contain a deleted 8.2; we record this without claiming scan verification. The transposed torsion map involves Gysin and cup product with d times the fixed polarization, so the factor d cannot be dropped.

6. R5: splitting lists checked with retained exact certificates; the symplectic supplement/complement distinction is explicit.
7. Lead D: full finite monodromy does not imply a nonzero coherent H2 obstruction on every proper base; on curves H2 vanishes.
8. Lead C: negative-one gluing alone is not a counterexample, because finite étale twisting can be effective.
9. E.7 is now independently audited: alpha=0 does not imply equality of the full lattices. E.10(a) is refuted integrally on the literal site; comparisons for a different modern site have not been substituted.

## Checkpoint 05: new results and exact scope

### A.1: a full coherent restriction counterexample in every prime

The unrestricted coherent assertion is now refuted. Starting with the explicitly described Lauritzen–Rao sixfold R, we independently compute its canonical bundle and identify H5(R,L^{-1}) with the dual of a concrete polynomial cokernel. The apolar functional based on (u0*z1-u1*z0)^(p-2) proves nonvanishing for every prime, rather than inferring a general statement from samples. A cyclic cover y^q=b, with q=2 for odd p and q=3 for p=2, turns that nonzero class into an actual restriction kernel. The pullback of L is very ample: the cover is the hypersurface y^q=B in the projective cone, which excludes the vertex. The branch is a fully specified generic form in 896 ambient coordinates over a specified perfect field. The Jacobian and Bertini arguments prove both smoothness assertions. Multiplication by y is an identity between two direct summands of the finite cyclic algebra, so the restriction kernel is nonzero. This also works for every smooth ay+s with a nonzero.

The failure occurs at degree one for this fixed embedding. The previously proved explicit high-degree bound still gives injectivity. The exact intermediate list, the surface case and the integral crystalline assertions are not inferred from this example and remain explicit obligations. The earlier report's statement that no actual coherent kernel had been verified is superseded.

### A.3–A.4: exact product invariants and effective full images

For X equal to a product of n ordinary elliptic curves with product polarization of degrees a_i>=3, the generic relative rank is d^n*product(a_i)-1 for every d>=1. If p divides every a_i*d, the entire geometric invariant covector space has dimension n for odd p and 2^n-1 for p=2. These are equalities, not lower bounds. The proof extends a covector across parameter-space divisors, identifies its lift with an endomorphism of the section space modulo scalars, and solves the Cartier identities using the character decomposition of Frobenius. A proposed intermediate shortcut asserting that Cartier roots preserve character spaces was rejected. The repaired proof raises the identity to the pth power, uses an eigenvector and the linear parameter coefficient, and proves character-space preservation instead. The correction is recorded as part of the audit.

Over F3 the explicit surface built from y²=x³+x²+1 has relative rank9d²-1 and exactly two arithmetic and geometric invariant covectors in every degree. Over F2 the analogous explicit ordinary product has exactly three in every positive even degree. Exact finite calculations give smooth ordinary sections in degrees one and two. The full image on the kernel of these fixed quotients is not claimed to be determined structurally.

A separate theorem gives a terminating exact algorithm for the complete geometric and arithmetic matrix groups from equations over a finite field, for every d>=max(1,reg(omega_X)-1). It constructs the finite étale algebra of Frobenius-fixed frames, obtains a primitive element from a bounded grid, factors by bounded finite polynomial enumeration, and tests every matrix by exact ideal preservation. Extending constants by degree |GL_r(Fp)| suffices to isolate the geometric components. Thus the construction also decides irreducibility. A fully specified extension to a finitely generated field of definition computes finite groups H_geom normal in H0 and a finite Galois constant field E. For any perfect base k, the arithmetic image is exactly rho^{-1}(Gal(E/(E intersection k))). The only residual field datum is that finite intersection; no universal computation over an unpresented noncomputable field is asserted. The report deliberately distinguishes this effective determination from a uniform description of all outputs as familiar finite groups. The latter remains the A.4 structural gate.

### B.3–B.4 and E.2

The higher wild characteristic-three argument proves that the maximum primitive formal valuation is divisible by three. It uses the Hesse-pencil cube-discriminant identity and a lower-ramification leading-coefficient argument. The resulting exact global minimum is e_min(n)=2*3^(2n-2). At each fixed e the largest possible bad full-torsion level lies between two explicit adjacent integers; except for the displayed one-level gap the answer is exact. For full9 the remaining indices are precisely24,30,42,48. This is a strictly smaller gate than the previous unrestricted higher-wild problem.

At p=2,e=1, the curve y²=x(x-1)(x+3) over Q2(zeta3) has E[4] isomorphic to mu4 direct sum Z/4, while its prime-to-2 inertia character differs from that of the split good group. Its discriminant valuation8 forces good-reduction ramification divisible by3, and the order-three trace is -1 instead of2. Therefore even manuscript level1 fails to determine the character in every height at least2. The precise minimum beyond this lower bound is still open.

For E.2, the characteristic-zero result extends to all flat quasi-coherent coefficients by a finite nilpotent filtration argument in the derived category. In characteristic p, a separate theorem covers all quasi-coherent coefficients on integral CM varieties with a smooth finite universal-homeomorphism cover. This includes the cusp k[t²,t³], whose Frobenius is not pure for any prime. The original Ben-Zvi–Nevins statements, including their ordinary pullback convention, were reopened and checked. General relative bases and arbitrary nonflat characteristic-zero coefficients remain open.

`code/coherent_restriction_counterexample.py` passed in0.668855 seconds. It checks all relevant monomial incidence relations for p=2,3,5,7,11,13, the characteristic-two40-to35 matrix of rank34, and cyclic multiplication. Generic smoothness and the all-prime conclusion use the written proofs. The root rerun of `ordinary_abelian_surface.py` took14.158152 seconds and verified four unit Jacobian ideals, Cartier rank36, relative rank35, four independent character components and seven F2-points. The degree-one certificate records the equation and Cartier matrix separately. The root rerun of `product_surface_obstruction.py` took0.047037 seconds and checked the F3 curve and its rational three-torsion.

The root independently read and reran `lang_frame_quartic.py` in0.186606 seconds. For the genuine family x4+y4+z4+x²yz+xz³+txy³+xyz², it verifies all three smoothness charts, its ordinary Hasse matrix, a six-dimensional frame algebra, all six GL2(F2) substitutions and a primitive polynomial. A simple Artin–Schreier pole proves geometric irreducibility, giving exactly diag(1,GL2(F2)) for this restricted family. This is not a claim about the full plane-quartic parameter space. The B.4 certificate checks all16 torsion points, all256 sums and all256 Galois compatibilities with exact arithmetic; a separate independent agent rerun passed. The wild-bound program checks the integer reductions within its stated finite range; it supplements the general proof.

All new theorem promotions follow independent proof checks. The paper and table retain six open main rows with narrower gates. Checkpoint production is not counted as mathematical movement, and the next scheduled substantive review remains due at06:50:40 UTC.


# Additional source and approach record for checkpoint 05

## A.1: why the new coherent counterexample answers a stronger question

The continuing searches concerned smooth very ample Kodaira counterexamples, restriction on the Picard scheme, Frobenius-killed coherent classes, and integral crystalline weak Lefschetz. Original full texts inspected include Lauritzen–Rao (1997), Section2 and its claim on pp3–5; Mukai's RIMS1736 (December2011), Theorems1–3; Totaro (2019), introduction and Theorem3.1; Ekedahl (1988), Proposition2.14 p120; Biswas–Holla, arXiv math/0603299v2, Section2 and Remark2.4; and Cotner–Zavyalov's Examples3.3.6/3.4.6. The exact endpoints and limitations are in the bibliography and census. These searches did not by themselves produce a verified smooth very ample surface with the required nonzero map. In particular negative line-bundle cohomology on a rational homogeneous variety cannot alone produce a kernel in its vanishing structure-sheaf cohomology.

The successful next approach was to change the ambient variety. A finite cyclic cover supplies a second summand in its structure-sheaf cohomology, and multiplication by the new homogeneous coordinate maps onto that summand identically. The explicit cone embedding verifies very ampleness. The all-prime cohomology of the sixfold was re-proved by an apolar functional, rather than delegated to a numerical sample or an unstated representation-theory result. This construction is credited as a derivation in this dossier using the opened Lauritzen–Rao example, without a priority claim. The original surface and full integral questions are retained.

Nakkajima–Yobuko arXiv1902.09110v3 was downloaded and read at Theorem6.10, hypotheses6.5 and Remark6.11, printed pp52–53. It supplies a precisely qualified integral weak-Lefschetz statement and a corrected large-degree proof. The lift/log hypotheses and the min(dim,p) range prevent using it to close the remaining arbitrary low-degree crystalline gate. The report does not silently remove those hypotheses.

## A.3–A.4: fixed covectors and a finite exact algorithm

Root reopened Sannai–Tanaka arXiv1411.5294v5 Lemma4.5 p11 and checked its Frobenius decomposition for ordinary abelian varieties. The product proof separately verifies ordinary SNC degeneration, all-degree normal generation, extension of invariant covectors across parameter divisors, and the exact character relations. The attempted assertion that taking a Cartier root preserves a Frobenius character space was rejected during audit. The revised proof establishes preservation by comparing a pth-power identity at an eigenvector and its first-order variation. This repair is essential to the exact invariant-space count.

The full-image algorithm was audited as an actual terminating procedure. No source was substituted for an unspecified Galois-group oracle. Its finite-field factorization step is bounded enumeration; its finitely generated field step is a shifted norm and square-free resultant; its absolute-factor step is a bounded coefficient ansatz followed by a proved terminating search in finite separable extensions. Root opened Stacks Tags037P,037Q,030W,030X, namely Lemmas10.47.8,10.47.13,10.44.2,10.44.3, and checked the needed finiteness, separability and geometric-integrality assertions. The finite field E is recovered from normalized factor coefficients, and its embedding in the selected frame component is computed by linear algebra.

The exact quartic-family test is a genuine smooth family, with three affine singularity ideals checked. The six-dimensional frame algebra has all six GL2(F2) actions, and a simple Artin–Schreier pole proves that it stays a field over algebraically closed constants. The algorithm gives an exact effective answer; a structural identification of all general-ambient groups is a distinct remaining objective. The product examples are now a concrete next test of that objective.

## B.3–B.4 and E.2

Anema–Top–Tuijp (2018), original SIGMA paper, Theorem1.1 p2 and Proposition5.1 pp4–5, was reopened. The former identifies the symplectic full-three-torsion Hesse family, and the latter gives the cube ratio of discriminants. Those exact statements support the invariant-differential step in the wild valuation argument. Root and the crystals agent independently checked the ramification calculation. The height-two level-four characteristic-two counterexample also passed an independent exhaustive group-law certificate. The reduction agent's log records its primary potential-good and supersingular-automorphism locators.

For E.2, Ben-Zvi–Nevins, original arXiv math/0212094v3, was reopened at Remark2.7 (pro-category tensor conventions), Proposition2.11, Theorem3.11, Theorem4.3 and Remark4.5. These identify ordinary pullback for the left-module/stratification equivalence; the claim is not inferred from their separate !-crystal result. Stacks Tag0CNF, Lemma29.47.9, was reopened for finite universal homeomorphisms and Frobenius powers. The arbitrary-flat characteristic-zero extension was independently checked against the previously opened Gaitsgory–Rozenblyum Corollary2.2.2 and Proposition3.4.3. A nilpotent filtration proves the ordinary flatness of every resulting value without a finite-generation assumption.

The full relative E.2 assertion is still under investigation. Ordinary tensor products cannot be replaced by completed tensor products in a descent argument without justification. In particular completion along the diagonal need not be faithfully flat over the uncompleted tensor product, so the tempting completed-nerve shortcut has not been used to claim a general theorem.

## Checkpoint 06: subsequent results and corrections

The table at the beginning of this report is the current status. Earlier checkpoint narratives below are dated research history; their former gates are superseded by the current table and this section. The work remains INCOMPLETE. In particular the broad E.2 assertion is now refuted, whereas the narrower manuscript insertion about a locally Noetherian base and coherent modules remains explicitly unresolved as a refinement.

### B.3: complete full-nine-torsion range

For p=3, an additive elliptic curve with full rational nine-torsion exists over a complete discretely valued field of absolute ramification e and perfect residue field if and only if 6 divides e and e>=18. All examples are over finite extensions of Q3. At the endpoint, E0:y²=x³-x over Q3(i) has division field L=Q3(i,E0[9]) of ramification72; its Z3[i]-module structure and exact primitive formal valuation1/72 prove this degree without an assumed local reciprocity dictionary. Taking the fixed field of the scalar i gives e18. A primitive formal parameter u transforms by i, and y²=x³-u4*x descends with all nine-torsion rational and exact defect4.

For every e=6d>18 the field is exactly K=Q3(i,eta,pi), where eta is a primitive ninth root and pi^d=eta-1. Its residue field is F9 and pi is a uniformizer. The displayed quadratic Hensel lift and a separately rescaled cubic Hensel lift supply three cube roots of (t-theta)/9 for theta=1,zeta,zeta². Fisher's original full-level equations and moduli interpretation then give E_t[9]=mu9 direct sum Z/9. The curve is y²+3txy+(t³-1)y=x³, with v(t)=9-e, v(j)=27 and v(Delta)=81-6e congruent9 modulo12. Thus it is potentially good but additive. The four former gaps e24,30,42,48 all have defect12. The proof explicitly avoids the invalid unrescaled Hensel inequality v(error)>2v(3); its integral rescaling has a simple linear reduction. The entire construction has independent parent and obstructions/crystals audits, with an independently executed exact symbolic certificate.

The fixed-e higher wild problem therefore starts at full27 and e216. Its previously proved one-level numerical bound and the sharp global ramification minimum remain valid. Higher-dimensional potentially good sharp thresholds remain open; the nine-torsion theorem does not assert them.

### E.2: counterexamples and relative positive theorem

Let I=Fp[t,t^-1]/Fp[t] and R=Fp[t] semidirect I with I²=0. Set s_n=(p^n-1)/(p-1), b_n=[t^-s_n] in I and X=Spec R[x]/(x^p-tx). The base is fully specified and non-Noetherian. The morphism is finite free of rankp, flat, finitely presented, and all its fibres are complete intersections. On any nilpotent test U inside T, choose n killing the p^n powers of its ideal and a local lift z of x. Multiplication by b_n*z^(p^n) defines a morphism delta of the structure crystal. Its definition is independent of every choice because t^(p^n)b_(n+1)=b_n. It is zero on X but nonzero on the finite free square-zero thickening T=Spec R[x]/(x^p-tx)^2, where it equals b1*x^p. As delta²=0, 1+delta is a nonidentity automorphism inducing the identity after restriction to stratifications. This is a direct proof on every infinitesimal test, independent of the Frobenius-divided comparison.

The same construction with the regular Noetherian base R0=Fp[t] and coefficient crystal O_T tensor_R0 I gives a nonzero morphism O_inf to that quasi-coherent crystal with zero restriction. This stronger variant uses noncoherent coefficients. It does not settle the manuscript's separate inserted restriction to a locally Noetherian base and coherent coefficients. That insertion is quoted from the supplied transcription, and the absent scans are not claimed to have been inspected.

The relative positive theorem proves that, over any Fp-algebra R, quasi-coherent infinitesimal crystals on a locally finitely presented X/R are equivalent to relative Frobenius-divided systems. When every relative Frobenius twist is pure, they are equivalent to ordinary stratified quasi-coherent modules. The proof uses finite free Frobenius on affine space, relative nilpotent envelopes, and effective pure module descent; it does not assume that R is perfect, reduced or Noetherian. As a concrete singular family, R[x,y]/(xy) satisfies the criterion for every Fp-algebra R via an explicit relative-Frobenius splitting.

For E:y²+xy=x³+1 over F2 and X=E×E with L=O_E(3O) external tensor O_E(3O), the geometric and arithmetic groups both equal GL8(F2) in degree one. In degree two both equal the entire pointwise stabilizer of the three previously constructed covectors, namely the matrices [A B;0 I3] with A in GL32(F2) and B an arbitrary32-by3 binary matrix. The argument certifies all divisorial inertia rather than extrapolating from point samples. On the whole projective linear system, including singular sections, the relative coherent bundle is the cotangent bundle and its Frobenius is represented by an explicitly constructed linear Cartier matrix. A line with ordinary leading coefficient meets every geometric determinant component. Exact finite-field ranks of M and M^[2]M at every root on the line prove stable rank loss exactly one at every generic Hasse divisor. A henselian finite Lang subgroup then fixes a hyperplane, so characteristic-two inertia consists of transvections. ### A.1: the surface coherent gate is closed

The subsequent surface construction removes the former dimension-two gate. For every prime p, a specified Artin–Schreier curve y^p-y=x^(hp-1), with h=8 at p=2 and h=p²-2 otherwise, has an explicitly computed Tango divisor and a globally generated (p+1)st root N. Its associated Raynaud cyclic-cover surface S has an ample globally generated line bundle L with H1(S,L^-1) nonzero. The proof checks smoothness, connectedness, every relevant eigensheaf, fibre intersections, and the numerical very-ampleness bound L^((p+1)^2).

A general basis of that very ample power defines simultaneous prime-to-p root covers. Their fibre product X is smooth, connected and finite flat over S. The pulled-back bundle A becomes very ample because the new root sections recover all affine coordinates of the original complete embedding. The explicit direct-sum formula for the finite pushforward preserves H1(S,L^-1) inside H1(X,A^-1). Hence every smooth hyperplane section Y has a nonzero kernel on H1(O_X) to H1(O_Y). This is a surface counterexample in every characteristic, with a fully specified generic coefficient field and embedding; the smooth sixfold from the preceding checkpoint remains an independent construction.

At p=2 the initial curve is y²+y=x15, of genus7, and N=O(2 infinity). The exact calculation gives h1(S,L^-1)=1 and H1(S,L^-r)=0 for all r>=2. Moreover h0(L)=6 and h0(L9)=556. Taking the556 ninth-root covers yields a very ample embedding into P561. The direct-sum formula then proves that the restriction kernel has dimension exactly1 in degree1 and0 in every degree>=2. ### A.4: degree three and two all-degree structural results

The later audited degree-three certificate gives geometric and arithmetic group GL80(F2). It uses two explicit ordinary sections, an irreducible nonreciprocal degree80 Frobenius polynomial, the prime4278255361 of multiplicative order80 for2, and an81-dimensional line certificate. An independent verifier reconstructs the matrices, computes both characteristic polynomials over the integers before reduction, checks primality by trial division, and repeats every finite-field rank calculation. The root rerun passed in4.011814542001957 seconds.

The same base certificate is used in an all-degree proof. Cubes of a very ample bundle separate second jets at one point and first jets at two points. For d>=4, a general pencil of degree-three curves is united with a fixed general ordinary degree-(d-3) curve. Incidence calculations separate simple tangency from the Hasse divisor and avoid all loci of codimension at least two. The exact structure-sheaf sequence computes the stable rank of each union and gives loss exactly one at every nonordinary parameter. An ordinary leading coefficient forces this pencil to meet every component of the full Hasse divisor. Thus every generic divisorial inertia group is generated by transvections, and purity gives transvection generation of geometric monodromy in every degree.

A separate argument classifies all invariant covectors on every characteristic-two product of ordinary elliptic curves, without the former parity restriction. Exact Cartier lifts are orthogonal idempotents on global sections. Perfectness of the Cartier pairing and global generation descend these to endomorphisms of F_*L^d. Odd-degree elliptic factors have stable rank-two Frobenius pushforward with scalar endomorphisms; each even-degree factor splits into two distinct character lines. Consequently the full invariant covector dimension is2^e-1, where e counts the even degrees among the factors. On the fixed surface it is0 for odd d and3 for even d. This identifies the entire fixed quotient but does not by itself identify the group on its kernel or all translations. Degrees4 onward remain the fixed-surface full-image gate.

## A.1: an investigated surface route that does not close the gate

Searches included the phrases very ample/Kodaira vanishing/surface/counterexample, H1/very ample/Raynaud, and crystalline/weak Lefschetz/counterexample. Its published metadata was checked against the institutional and publisher records: *Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra*,221(10),2431–2444 (2017), DOI10.1016/j.jpaa.2016.12.030. The original Yukihide Takayama arXiv:0805.0524v4 was also opened. Zheng explicitly corrects several claims of that earlier work; uncorrected ranges were not used.

The following obstruction was derived for the explicit polarizations in Zheng's Theorem3.7. Its cyclic-cover surface has a geometric cuspidal fibre F with affine ring k[u^ell,u^p], and the ramification section meets the smooth point at infinity. The ample line bundle Z_(a,b) restricts to O_F(a infinity). The theorem's nonvanishing range has1<=a<=ell-1 and ell dividing p+1. If ell is a proper divisor, a<min(ell,p), so the restricted line bundle has only constants as sections. If ell=p+1, then a<=p; all a<p still give constants, and a=p gives only the two-dimensional space spanned by1 andu^p. None embeds this cuspidal fibre. Therefore these particular nonvanishing polarizations are not very ample and do not supply the surface version of the cyclic-cover restriction counterexample. This argument does not rule out other polarizations or surface constructions. It is a recorded failed route, not claimed movement in A.1.

### A.1(a),(b): explicit integral counterexamples for every prime

For a smooth proper geometrically connected V, write q=h1(O_V), h10=h0(Omega1_V), b=rank_W H1_cris and t=dim H2_cris[p]. Take the previously constructed very ample surface (X,A) with a=h1(A^-1)>0, form Z=X times P1, and embed it with B=A external tensor O(m). For every smooth Y in |B|, the divisor sequence and Kunneth give q(Y)=q(X)+a(m-1). Rational crystalline weak Lefschetz identifies the two first crystalline ranks and makes H2(Z) to H2(Y) rationally injective. Therefore t(Y)-t(Z)>=a(m-1)-h10(X). Choose m so that this is positive. The torsion group on Y then needs strictly more generators than the source torsion, so restriction is not surjective on torsion. Rational injectivity identifies im(u) intersect T(Y) with u(T(Z)); the resulting nonzero torsion quotient embeds in coker(u). Both asserted integral conclusions fail.

The construction is numerical, not conditional on an unknown dimension. For every prime, put ell=p+1, q0=ell², n0=2 at p2 and n0=p(p-2) otherwise, and g=1+p*ell*n0/2. The first tame cover has at most Bp=g+p+2+p³(p+1)n0/2 global one-forms. The r simultaneous q0th-root covers give h10(X)<=q0^r(Bp+r), so m=q0^r(Bp+r)+2 produces the integral counterexample. The all-prime formulas and local differential inclusions were independently audited, and the arithmetic verifier was independently run for p2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19.

### A.4: a conditional uniform group theorem with one geometric hypothesis

### A.4: eventual geometric and arithmetic groups for every ordinary elliptic pair

Let E1 and E2 be any ordinary elliptic curves over a perfect field of characteristic two, let X=E1×E2, and use the product of their cubic polarizations. There is a terminating procedure producing an integer d1 such that, in every odd degree d>=d1, both monodromy groups are GL_(9d²-1)(F2). In every even degree d>=d1, both are the full pointwise stabilizer of the three independent invariant covectors. Writing r=9d²-1, this consists of all matrices [A B;0 I3], with A in GL_(r-3)(F2) and arbitrary B. The representation is irreducible exactly in odd degree. The determinant character is trivial because the coefficient field is F2. This extends the previously completed fixed-product theorem to every ordinary elliptic pair.

The threshold is explicit through a finite terminating search. Enumerate chains of 3-isogenies E_i'→E_i until the product of the source curves has full degree-one GL8 monodromy, as decided by the already proved exact finite frame-cover algorithm. If the resulting odd degrees are m1,m2, take d1=max(m1,m2)+1. This is a terminating algorithm on an effective field of definition, and an existence construction over an arbitrary perfect field; no closed numerical bound uniform in the two elliptic curves is asserted. Chai(1995), Theorem2, printedp477, proves density of the fixed-prime ordinary Hecke orbit over every algebraically closed field. The checked geometric-integrality spreading lemma, Stacks Tag0559, Lemma37.27.5, supplies the nonempty open set of full-GL8 pairs that this search must meet.

There are two geometric steps. First, a universal one-factor Cartier calculation on y²+xy=x³+A x²+B, B nonzero, gives a constant invertible symmetrizer. Tensoring it gives a symmetric nine-dimensional pencil whose diagonal entries are independent coordinates. Its determinant contains the full squarefree diagonal monomial with coefficient one; every nonidentity matching term has a squared factor. This proves that the degree-one Hasse divisor is geometrically reduced. Uniform two-point jet bounds and a mixed-tacnode argument then show that the Hasse divisor is geometrically irreducible and reduced in every degree d>=2, with generic stable-rank drop exactly one. The common kernel of all invariant covectors is irreducible in every such degree. These assertions do not require finding the isogeny threshold.

Second, a generic degree-one curve on E1'×E2' has an ordinary nodal image under the odd product isogeny. The proof verifies double-point transversality and excludes triple points, including the loci where one translation coordinate is zero. The image has the exact divisor class O(3m2O) external tensor O(3m1O); the norm calculation controls the Picard-zero part as well. Adding a fixed grid realizes a degeneration in every degree d>=d1. The degree-one GL8 quotient can be isolated as an actual block acting trivially on a complement: the remaining node covers have symmetric-group factors of degree at most18, and their groups have no prime31, whereas GL8 has such a factor. The previously checked Goursat and first-cohomology arguments split the block. Transvection-group classification and the full translation-subgroup calculation then give the stated groups. All three invariant covectors in even degree are defined over the original perfect field, so the arithmetic group is the same pointwise stabilizer.

### A.4: full degree-one monodromy despite a double Hasse component

The same supersingular product has geometric and arithmetic degree-one image GL8(F2) over every perfect characteristic-two base. In tensor coefficient coordinates s with3×3 matrixS, its relative Hasse polynomial is

    h(s)=det(S)²·(s^[2]t (J3 tensor J3) s),

where J3 reverses the three basis coordinates. The determinantal cubic and the second, smooth cubic are geometrically irreducible and distinct. Thus a double Hasse component is compatible with full geometric monodromy.

The proof derives the Cartier pencil from C(1)=0, C(x)=1, C(y)=x, C(xy)=y and the zero values on squares. After reversing the tensor basis it is the Hessian of detS. Its nine maximal Pfaffians are det(S) times the coefficient vector. The adjugate formula gives the determinant on the relative Euler-sequence hyperplane exactly, including both factors and their multiplicities.

Two explicit F8 points complete the group argument. The first has relative Frobenius polynomial T8+T7+T5+T+1, irreducible and nonreciprocal; an independent restriction-of-scalars27×27 characteristic-polynomial calculation confirms it. The second lies on the simple cubic component and has relative stable rank seven. Along an explicit tangent direction the determinant has a simple zero, and the first derivative on the one-dimensional Frobenius kernel has a nonzero component in the seven-dimensional stable subspace. A complete local lemma turns this into a wild transvection: lift the seven unit directions over a strict trait, write the last Frobenius column as (b(t),a(t)) with a of order one, and solve the Lang lift by Artin–Schreier equations with right side b/a². A nonzero simple pole forces ramification and hence a rank-one unipotent inertia element. Its normal closure, together with the irreducible nonreciprocal Frobenius element, is GL8 by the already checked transvection classification. The dense smooth-open restriction preserves the image; the two coefficient certificates do not require an additional claim that those particular curves are smooth.

An order-four inertia element has traces h-2 and h because its elliptic eigenvalues are i,-i. The manuscript truncation is M(nu)=M[p^(nu+1)], so failure at3^N gives least universal index at leastN. This is the wild maximum already checked in25000 exact integer comparisons. It improves the tame lower bound, for example to2 at e24 and3 at e216, in every height at least two. It is a lower bound, not a claimed exact least index for arbitrary pairs.

## Research searches and unproved directions

The root queried both engines for generic p-rank of ample curves on a fixed surface, Cartier nilpotent forms, generic ordinarity of arbitrary hypersurface sections, and generic Cartier rank on an abelian surface. Most results concerned full moduli, special covers, or normalization formulas. The 2017 paper Lefschetz theorems for torsion algebraic cycles in codimension2 (DOI10.1016/J.AIM.2017.05.018) appeared with a conditional Illusie statement requiring ordinary linear complete intersections on the ambient variety. A search-snippet sentence about generic complete intersections was not imported as an arbitrary fixed-ambient theorem. The primary theorem has not been used from that snippet. The Koblitz original and previously audited Illusie results remain distinguished from the unresolved structural generic-rank formula.

Two further approaches remain exploratory. One is a theta-group symmetrizer on an arbitrary ordinary principally polarized abelian surface in characteristic two, using the level-three Heisenberg representation; its required jet-rank strata have not yet been proved. The other transports a full GL80 seed through a general odd isogeny. It requires control of self-tacnode and triple-point boundary divisors and of the full node permutation images; the product-isogeny argument alone does not prove those statements. Neither approach is promoted or counted as a result.

The all-degree supersingular rank proof and supersingular degree-one full group proof passed independent root re-proofs. The even-degree obstruction uses an inclusion of finite groups X[2]→P[2] before applying Verschiebung; it never assumes an inclusion X→P. The fullGL8 proof separately establishes geometric transvection inertia and handles the normal closure in the arithmetic group.

## Supersingular invariant covectors and actual linear blocks

The root read supersingular_exact_covectors.tex completely and independently rederived every step. The linearized image already has the stable rank in both parities. An arbitrary invariant covector lifts uniquely after one Frobenius-root extension; its square is rational, has no divisorial poles, and is a global quadratic section. The common kernel of all Cartier coefficients is zero by the perfect Cartier pairing and global generation of the Frobenius pushforward. Comparing monomials of odd exponent kills all quadratic cross terms. The resulting linear operator descends to an endomorphism of F_*N. Odd-degree simplicity and the even-degree nonsplit unipotent algebra leave exactly0 and1 relative invariant covectors, respectively. The unique even covector is defined overF2, so geometric and arithmetic invariant spaces agree. This is a complete covector calculation, not a full image classification.

The root also read supersingular_uniform_GL8_block.tex completely. In odd degree the quaternion norm supplies a matching odd self-isogeny; product jet and triple-value incidences give generic nodal images in the exact desired line bundle. In even degree the intersection cover with a fixed sharp odd member has full symmetric group, using double transitivity and a section with exactly one double zero. ## Theta jets, their source scope, and the next monodromy extension

Both search engines were used for three-theta jet separation, two-point first jets, characteristic-two Kummer separation, and higher embeddings of abelian surfaces. The root wrote a complete direct proof in sections/A_ppav_two_jets.tex. It includes an elementary all-characteristic dichotomy for principally polarized abelian surfaces; exact second-jet surjectivity for a smooth genus-two theta divisor; two-first-jet ranks6 off a dimension-two locus, at least5 off a dimension-one81-curve locus, and at least4 everywhere; finite exceptional second points for each fixed first point on an ordinary surface; and an irreducible discriminant with generic integral one-node member. A three-theta product separates any three distinct values in the smooth-theta case. A generic sum of three theta translates with parameter sum zero gives an ordinary nodal member, hence ordinary generic members in every positive degree. The obstruction/crystal agent independently audited all proofs, including the later dichotomy, ordinary-member and three-value additions.

## A fixed mixed surface over a perfect function field

The root read A3_mixed_generic_ranks.tex and its code completely. The proof passes: in the smooth elliptic family y²+txy+y=x³, the relative coherent quotient is a vector bundle of constant rank across the supersingular fibre t0. For each odd degree its invertibility there forces invertibility at the same generic t; no countable intersection of opens or new choice of the elliptic factor is made. In even degree the connected Verschiebung-kernel inclusion in the Prym supplies the upper bound and a union of two sharp odd members supplies the lower bound. Thus the fixed surface overF2(t)^perf has relative ranks9d²−1 odd and9d²−2 even. The same holds for every transcendental ordinary j. The arbitrary algebraic ordinary-factor question remains open; bounded explicitF2 probes are not promoted to an all-degree proof.

## Completed ordinary-ppav structural extension,10:14UTC

The combined ordinary_ppav_surface_full_groups.tex has now passed three independent complete proof audits: root, obstruction/crystal, and reduction/descent. Every ordinary principally polarized abelian surface in characteristic two is included after the stated terminating threshold, not just products. The exact invariant quotient is0odd/3even; the common kernel is irreducible fromd2 and the Hasse divisor is irreducible/reduced with generic stable loss one. A full degree-one open in moduli follows from the connected frame cover of the certified product seed and normality after a finite base normalization. A polarized odd isogeny from that open gives a generic nodal image, with exact norm line bundle corrected by a fixed geometric two-torsion translation. The fixed added divisor has pullback an integral ample curve, whose intersection permutation group is the full symmetric group. The entire graph-plus-constant image has no GL8 composition factor, and Goursat with the proved H1 vanishing supplies an actual block. Transvection classification, common-kernel irreducibility and absence of invariant vectors yield the entire groups.

The auxiliary isogeny is explicitly permitted over a finite extension of the original perfect field. Arithmetic descent is kept over the original field: in even degree its entire image is the preimage of the Galois permutation subgroupGamma on the three nonzero Frobenius-kernel characters. The ambient threshold adds reg(I_A)−1, so no characteristic-two projective-normality theorem is silently assumed. The threshold is a terminating algorithm over effective fields of definition, not a numerical bound independent of the surface.

The ordinary open and an etale-local nonsymmetric representative of the polarization suffice, avoiding an inseparable symmetric-theta torsor in characteristic two.

## Checkpoint 11: universal surface ranks and nonordinary invariant quotients

## Current state

This checkpoint remains **INCOMPLETE**. The open main rows remain A.3, A.4, B.3 in higher dimension, and B.4. No arbitrary-ambient classification is inferred from the new abelian-surface theorems. This note records only fully audited mathematics; pending further candidates are listed separately.

## Exact rank formula for all principal surfaces

For every principally polarized abelian surface (A,Theta) in characteristic two, let L=3Theta and let f_A be its geometric2-rank. In the complete linear system |L^d|, every positive degree has generic relative stable rank9d²−1 when d is odd and9d²−3+f_A when d is even. The coherent relative dimension is9d²−1. Thus Frobenius is generically bijective precisely in odd degree or when A is ordinary. This closes the previously explicit algebraic mixed-factor refinement, including every ordinary j-invariant. For the fixed ambient embedding, surjective restriction is guaranteed at d≥max(1,reg(I_A)−1); products have surjective restriction in every degree. The entire proof, including the exceptional Pfaffian tensors, the relative determinant, odd norm construction and even connected-Prym bound, passed root and independent monodromy audits.

## Entire invariant quotients on nonordinary principal surfaces

For every nonordinary principally polarized abelian surface in characteristic two, the complete geometric and arithmetic invariant-covector spaces have dimension0 in every odd degree and2^{f_A} in every even degree. In particular the two-rank-zero cases both have one covector, including the nonzero nilpotent chain, and the two-rank-one cases have two. The arithmetic action on these invariant spaces is trivial over the original perfect field. The proof handles an arbitrary persistent nilpotent length before reducing to the entire four-dimensional distribution algebra of the Frobenius kernel. Both other Part-A agents independently audited the complete proof, its relative-Frobenius conventions, the local identities and arithmetic descent. The whole group in these general nonordinary families remains open.

## Two further exact supersingular groups

On the fixed product E0×E0, E0:y²+y=x³ overF2, with the cubic Segre embedding, the degree-two rank is33 and both complete images areF2^{32} semidirect GL32(F2), the full pointwise stabilizer of the unique covector. The proof uses one irreducible nonreciprocal degree32 Frobenius polynomial with primitive prime65537, and a second literal matrix witness showing that an arithmetic Frobenius has no fixed lift of the invariant quotient. The already proved actual geometricGL8 block and the self-normalizing-complement argument force the full geometric group.

The degree-three geometric and arithmetic groups are bothGL80(F2). Its retained Frobenius certificate has an irreducible nonreciprocal degree80 polynomial with primitive prime4278255361. Together with the same actual geometric block this gives the entire group. These two proofs passed independent root and reduction/descent audits. Exact full groups in degrees one through three are settled; no conclusion for every higher degree is inferred from the finite searches.

## The height-two comparison graph

In the remaining norm-one, potentially supersingular height-two comparison with different tame special-inertia orders, a level3^n isomorphism forces the special graph at every smaller level r to be ker(F_M^r)×ker(F_N^r). Its rank-nine successive finite-flat quotients have special fibre alpha3²; multiplication by3 is generically an isomorphism and specially zero. This is proved using integral pairings on full Barsotti–Tate groups, flat graph orthogonality and tame projectors. It is not by itself counted as a new numerical exclusion of a least index.

## Checkpoint 12: coherent crystals and inseparable surface polarizations

## Current state

## Coherent crystals over a Noetherian base

For every flat locally finitely presented morphism X→S with S locally Noetherian, restriction gives an equivalence between ordinary coherent stratified modules and quasi-coherent infinitesimal crystals whose value on X is coherent. The statement holds on both the small and big infinitesimal sites, including arbitrary classical tests, and in every characteristic. Values are coherent on Noetherian tests and finitely presented on arbitrary tests. The coefficient module need not be flat.

The proof establishes a universally exact completed augmented Cech complex by filtering along the nilpotent test ideal. This descends finite Hom modules and proves ordinary full faithfulness. Flatness of the completed formal-nerve projections lifts the coherent stratification to derived complete data. Jiang's precisely checked comparison yields a derived crystal. A finite nilpotent filtration proves that its values are in D≤0; taking H0 then gives ordinary Cartesian pullback. The proof does not claim that the intermediate derived crystal is discrete. Finite-type graph neighbourhoods, common refinements and equalizers extend it to arbitrary tests. The root, monodromy and reduction/descent agents independently checked the entire proof and its original source bridge.

The prior nonfaithfulness examples are unchanged: dropping coherence can fail even over a regular Noetherian base, and dropping the Noetherian condition can fail for a rank-one structure crystal. Their scope remarks now point to the proved narrower theorem, rather than describing it as undecided.

## Every polarization on an ordinary surface

Let A be an ordinary abelian surface in characteristic two, let M be any ample line bundle, put D=chi(M), and use the embedding L=M³. For every positive d the geometric generic smooth curve in |L^d| is ordinary of genus 9Dd²+1, and its relative stable rank is exactly 9Dd²−1. No parity restriction on D or d remains.

The integral dual polarization is constructed by descent along lambda_M. In its two-primary kernel, the connected multiplicative factor is maximal isotropic. Choosing it makes the dual principal-source isogeny finite etale even when its degree is even. A sharp genus-ten ordinary source curve has a nodal norm image; the collision incidence proof is checked for even-order translations. An arbitrary target translation puts the norm in the exact desired linear system. Transverse unions of ordinary members then prove every degree. The existing ambient regularity bound remains explicit; no assertion about an arbitrary embedding being a cube is made.

## Sharp ranks for inseparable supersingular product types

On A=E×E, E:y²+y=x³ in characteristic two, let M=O_E(aO) external O_E(bO), where a,b are positive integers, and put L=M³. If exactly one factor is even and that integer has 2-adic valuation one, the generic relative ranks are 9abd²−2 for odd d and 9abd²−3 for even d. If both a,b are even, the rank is 9abd²−3 for every d. The coherent relative dimension is 9abd²−1. Types with exactly one even factor of higher 2-adic valuation are not covered by this theorem.

The proof first obtains global Cartier-kernel relations from the canonical connection on an even-degree factor. An exact (6,3) base matrix has rank(C)=rank(C²)=16. Odd-degree product isogenies propagate this sharp base, with a complete nodality proof allowing kernel projections that are not injective. Transverse unions of two sharp odd product types give the both-even lower bound. The complete independent audit also reconstructed all eighteen matrix columns from the curve-ring identity f=a²+x b², without importing the author's monomial Cartier formula.

## The supersingular global contact witness

The local self-tacnode and triple-point Cartier lemmas are now proved after full independent audits. One global norm-family witness has also been certified over GF64. Its source is geometrically smooth; its degree-three norm image has exactly one simple self-tacnode and otherwise ordinary nodes. The relative Hasse divisor is smooth at this image. The exact coefficient vector is (38,14,10,47,47,43,30,4,8), in the specified monomial tensor basis. All four smooth-source charts and all144 collision ideals were checked over the algebraic closure, with genuine rational translation identities and nilpotent-support tests. A separate truncated elliptic-addition calculation verifies the simple-contact coefficient55 and mixed Cartier value60.

## The remaining height-two character test is elliptic

For p=3, absolute ramification e=2 and height h=2, the least manuscript index remains either2 or3; 81-torsion always suffices. Every potentially supersingular norm-one comparison in the remaining case can now be realized by elliptic curves, preserving the integral Tate lattice and the special inertia action. The proof uses explicit integral quaternion conjugacy, labelled Serre–Tate deformation, algebraization and generic Galois descent. It does not descend a good model across ramification.

For a potentially supersingular elliptic curve, the tame special-inertia quotient has order t=4/gcd(4,v(Delta)). Thus the residual level27 ambiguity is equivalent to two triples (a2,a4,a6) over W(k)[pi]/(pi²−3), for an algebraically closed field k of characteristic three, with 0≤v(Delta)≤23, 3v(c4)>v(Delta), isomorphic generic27-torsion, and discriminant valuations in different columns of {0 mod4,2 mod4,odd}. This is a proved six-coefficient criterion. Its existence or nonexistence has not been decided.

## Checkpoint 13: uniform rectangular ranks and residual character restrictions

The current outcome table supersedes earlier checkpoint gates. This is an interim checkpoint, marked INCOMPLETE. The next actual hourly review is due at12:50:40UTC; checkpoint packaging is not counted as mathematical movement.

## A.3: every ordinary embedding and every supersingular rectangle

For an ordinary abelian surface in characteristic two, the cube-embedding restriction has been removed. If M is any ample line bundle, D=chi(M), and n>=3, a geometric generic smooth member of |M^n| is ordinary, has genus Dn²+1, and has relative stable rank Dn²−1. For the embedding defined by M, the ambient degree bound is explicitly n>=max(3,reg(I_A)−1). The proof treats every principal multiple, including degree four jet exceptions and even-degree etale norm kernels, and then uses the proved ordinary principal-source norm construction. No statement about |M| or |M²| is inferred. The full proof passed root, monodromy and reduction/descent audits. The arithmetic certificate checks254 values of n and32512(n,D) identities; author runtime0.012083560999599285s and independent reduction/descent runtime0.013041352001891937s are retained.

The supersingular product result is now uniform in every product polarization type. On E² with E:y²+y=x³, for M=O(aO) external-product O(bO), L=M³, and every positive d,

    r_d = 9abd² − 1 − epsilon(ad) − epsilon(bd),

where epsilon(c)=1 for even c and0 for odd c. The genus is9abd²+1 and the relative coherent dimension is9abd²−1. The same complete-system rank applies to the ambient hypersurface family for d>=max(1,reg(I_A)−1). Thus both odd factors give rank9abd²−1, one even factor gives9abd²−2, and two even factors give9abd²−3. The earlier restriction on the two-adic valuation of the even factor is eliminated.

The infinite calculation is proved by a kernel sheaf, not by extrapolating finite matrices. For q divisible six, the sparse section in type(2q,3) gives a map V³→(det V)³, where V=F_*O(2qO). Its kernel is the trace-zero endomorphism bundle modified at exactly two reduced F4 points. The two global classes in End(V)/scalars are multiplication by source x and the invariant derivative. Requiring each to preserve the rank-one image line gives independent conditions at the two points; consequently the kernel has h0=2 and h1=0. The two kernel vectors are s and its first-factor derivative. Their map to the two-dimensional cokernel has matrix [[zeta,1],[zeta²,1]], determinant1. This proves both rankC and rankC² equal6q−2 for every q divisible six. Odd-degree etale norms and the earlier parity constructions give the complete formula above.

All source/base Frobenius conventions and both local elementary modifications were checked independently. Author, root and reduction/descent complete certificate runtimes are0.1617353309993632s,0.154388964001555s and0.1660513059978257s. The eight independently reconstructed matrices have q=6,12,18,24,30,48,96,192. The uniform proof uses none of those finite cases as an induction assumption. The discovery programs, rejected patterns, the nonsharp cases in q=3..96, and the initial SymPy-integer JSON serialization failure are all retained. The earlier dual-kernel diagnostic took0.30682451300526736s and is explicitly a finite diagnostic.

The unresolved A.3 scope is arbitrary smooth projective X and the remaining nonordinary inseparable polarization types outside these proved families.

## A.4: the degree-three Hasse divisor

The degree-three relative Hasse divisor of the fixed supersingular cubic product is geometrically irreducible and reduced. The proof uses the degree-nine norm map, the source factorization D²Q, the affine kernel action of order216, one self-tacnode witness and two tangent-triple witnesses representing the two unordered triple orbits. The exact orbits have sizes12 and72. The pair incidence is generically a P4 bundle and the triple incidence a P5 bundle; exceptional jet loci have no additional divisorial component.

The conductor calculation gives the full formula g(Z)−f(Z)=sum(g(C_i)−f(C_i))+sum(delta_x−r_x+1). This proves that every generic collision divisor maps into the target Hasse divisor. At the generic source determinant divisor the graph cohomology is Frobenius-unit over the local ring, so its pullback multiplicity is exactly two. The three local bridge criteria place the source cubic and all collision factors in one target component. Any additional target component would pull back with degree at most six, contradicting the norm pullback degree9*deg(H). A smooth Hasse point proves reducedness.

Every successful source was checked on all four projective charts, and every possible pair or triple collision was checked over the algebraic closure by exact ideal certificates. The first two failed contact witnesses are retained as failures. The two successful tangent-triple collision checks took72.36891810200177s and69.24018129799515s; independent reruns took76.3690687260023s and74.86146398200071s. The complete local and source-smoothness outputs, including actual runtimes, remain beside the programs. The root kernel-orbit rerun took0.006542789000377525s, and the three main-incidence ranks are exactly6,6,6.

The degree-three full group GL80(F2) was already proved by a separate certificate. This new divisor theorem does not imply a uniform higher-degree full-image theorem.

The uniform contact-source existence gate has also been closed. For every translation with both elliptic coordinates nonzero, an explicit irreducible Artin–Schreier coefficient family supplies a smooth global source with a simple prescribed contact and unequal values of its extra Cartier-killed form. In the nonflex case the local coefficient is T(c⁴+c). The full source-smoothness proof classifies all singularity incidences in its P4 contact slice. The degree54 full discriminant restricts with the four forced factors F³T³h³v² and one remaining irreducible factor of total degree43. The irreducible degree3 Hasse cubic cannot be that factor, so its generic source is globally smooth. The local and global proofs passed a complete root audit; the exact universal local certificate passed in0.34270756500336574s (author) and0.36782622399914544s (root). The program explicitly tests local identities only; the global conclusion comes from the written discriminant proof. Further collisions under a prescribed norm map and uniform tangent-triple bridges remain genuine unresolved gates.

## B.4: scalar residual exclusion and a smaller cyclic-four gate

At p=3,e=2,h=2, the least index remains in{2,3}: 81-torsion suffices, and the undecided test is27-torsion. The new scalar exclusion is already valid for9-torsion. After a simultaneous quadratic twist, a hypothetical remaining27 comparison has residual image either nontrivial unipotent C3 or irreducible tame C4.

The scalar proof reads Fisher's original full-level Hesse family and Theorem4.3. The reverse equation has the essential factor3. Its correct valuation shift is two modulo three, and it leaves two opposite-character valuation patterns, B/A and D/E. Neither is excluded merely by valuations. Each is excluded by an exact unit calculation: a required cube congruent to one would have deviation valuation one, whereas any such cube has deviation valuation at least three at absolute ramification two. ## Checkpoint 14 work: the residual cyclic-four gate

This is ongoing work after the immutable checkpoint13. The work remains INCOMPLETE. No new checkpoint is due before13:20:40UTC.

## Proved restrictions after checkpoint13

For mixed elliptic products E_ord×E_ss in characteristic two and the cube of an arbitrary product polarization of type(a,b), the geometric generic relative stable rank is9abd²−1−epsilon(ad) for everyd>=2. The same formula holds atd1 unlessa is even andb=1. The full geometric proof uses arbitrary-degree ordinary etale sources, odd supersingular etale sources, the already proved cubic nodal-norm theorem and a transverse odd-plus-odd union. The even ordinary factor supplies the global additional Cartier kernel. Root and monodromy complete proof audits passed; the original AV5.20–5.22 and5.26 passages were read. The author/root arithmetic runtimes are0.03129147599975113s and0.03777776699280366s. This is an infinite-family theorem, not an extrapolation from the retained identities.

B39 first narrows a normalized unipotent residual comparison: the common three-division field is generated by a cube root of a noncube unit; the opposite tame orders are4 and2, with j-valuations3 and>=6. Every nonunit cube class is excluded by the exact reverse/direct unit deviations4,5,7 over the cubic extension. The scalar-unit depth proof is given explicitly by Hensel's equation w³+w+pi*w²=b. ### A.3: mixed surfaces beyond products

For a mixed abelian surface in characteristic two, write a(M) for the index of its polarization on the rank-one etale2-adic Tate module. Integral Dieudonne duality gives two paired elementary-divisor indices a(M),b(M), with v2(chi(M))=a(M)+b(M). The dual polarization chi(M)lambda_M^(-1) is integral, including inseparable polarizations. A prescribed etale principal norm source of degree chi(M) exists exactly when a(M)=0. In this class, for L=M³ and every d>=1, the generic relative stable rank is9chi(M)d²−1 in odd degree and9chi(M)d²−2 in even degree. The proof does not assume a product decomposition or odd chi(M). An even-degree Prym upper bound is also proved for every mixed polarization. The a(M)>0 class remains outside this theorem.

For every finite odd subgroup of the fixed supersingular elliptic product whose two coordinate projections are injective, and every nonzero kernel difference, there is a globally smooth cubic source on its Hasse cubic whose norm image has exactly one simple self-tacnode and otherwise only ordinary nodes. The extra Cartier-kernel differential has unequal values at the identified tangents. The proof treats every moving pair and triple incidence, not merely a finite list of torsion points. ### B.4: the smallest odd-prime height-two case is sharp

Theorem B-RD42 proves nu_min(3,2,2)=2 for the full permitted height-two class:27-torsion determines the requested character on prime-to-three inertia, whereas the explicit9-torsion ambiguity proves sharpness. ## Checkpoint 15 work: all odd supersingular-product groups

The principal advance is a complete full-image theorem for every odd degree on the fixed supersingular product E² in characteristic two, with E:y²+y=x³ and its (3,3) embedding. The geometric and arithmetic groups are GL_(9d²−1)(F2) for every odd d>=1. The uniform even-degree and arbitrary-X problems remain open.

## Uniform tangent triples and odd-degree component allocation

The new third-value source-discriminant lemma proves that every required third-value hyperplane contains globally smooth sources with both source Hasse factors nonzero. A normalized-row construction gives simple contact of two branches and a transverse third, on the same irreducible rank-five incidence. The projected value map, its degree-two pencil poles, and the order-three pole-cancellation exception then exclude every other kernel collision uniformly. The cyclic three-element case uses the previously completely certified collinear witness only inside its subgroup, while the new incidence proof excludes all outside collisions. Root, reduction/descent and obstruction/crystal complete audits all passed.

The arbitrary-odd-degree assembly proves that the norm pullback has only the source cubic factors and pair/triple collision factors; the determinant factor D has multiplicity exactly two. Mixed-contact and tangent-triple smooth points assign all collision factors and Q to one target Hasse component. A further component would pull back to degree at most6, contradicting d²>=9. A sharp-source tacnode gives generic stable rank loss one. The relative coherent bundle is Omega1 on projective space, so determinant allocation and the exact absence of odd-degree invariant covectors give irreducibility. Purity and local Lang theory give transvection generation. The already proved actual natural GL8 block excludes every form-preserving alternative in Kantor–Seress Theorem3.6, original printedp22, which was actually viewed again by all auditors. This proves the full group without a finite-degree extrapolation.

## Dyadic eight-torsion ambiguity

B43 gives an explicit quotient of an elliptic curve with a rational point of order8 over the unramified quadratic extension of Q2, together with its exact Miller-function Kummer class q=−4lambda/3. Its8-torsion agrees with a Tate group, while the special-inertia characters differ on an order-three quotient element. The complete curve, point multiples, invariant calculations and Kummer identity are checked in retained exact programs. The lower bound nu_min(2,e,h)>=3 holds for3 not dividing e and h>=2. No16-torsion sufficiency is claimed.

## Additional mixed-product rank work

A fixed (6,3) section on every ordinary-times-supersingular product has a16minor of its twice-iterated dual Frobenius matrix equal to c^5, where c is the nonzero ordinary Weierstrass parameter. The complete p-basis identities and tensor Cartier matrix are derived symbolically. The exact search retains all six trials, including unsuccessful vectors; the independent verifier retains its initial software-domain coercion failure and corrected monic pseudo-remainder run. A proposed arbitrary-degree ordinary-axis norm transfer was invalid: it gives class(6,3n), whereas the required class(6n,3) comes from the supersingular axis and requires n odd for etaleness. The corrected nodal-incidence argument is written and independently audited. The current outcome table records promotion only after both seed and norm files have actually passed their independent audits.

## Checkpoint 16 work: all supersingular-product groups and all mixed-product ranks

This checkpoint advances the proved gates in A.3, A.4, and B.4. The general questions remain explicitly open. All results below were subjected to complete independent proof audits; finite computations certify only their stated algebraic scope.

## All degrees on the fixed supersingular product

For E:y²+y=x³ in characteristic two, X=E² and L=O(3O) external-tensor O(3O), the geometric and arithmetic relative images now agree in every degree. In odd degree they are GL_(9d²−1)(F2). In even degree they are the full stabilizer of the unique invariant covector, F2^(9d²−4) semidirect GL_(9d²−4)(F2), acting in rank9d²−3. The unique proper nonzero invariant subspace in the even case is its covector kernel.

The new even proof identifies the first Frobenius image and its negative reflexive extension. A reduced irreducible determinant for the finite intersection algebra on an odd boundary has degree18ae+9e². Two odd decompositions force irreducibility and reducedness of the global unit-Hasse form for every even degree at least four; the degree-four comparison uses the irreducible restriction factor of degree135. The exact degree-two theorem and the previous all-odd theorem complete all degrees. The marked contact incidence may be inseparable in characteristic two: reducedness is proved from the finite algebra itself, not inferred from separability. Root, monodromy, and the other two agents independently checked the whole argument.

## All mixed elliptic-product ranks, without a modulus exception

For every ordinary elliptic curve E_o, every supersingular elliptic curve E_s, every perfect characteristic-two field and all positive integers a,b,d, the product system O(3ad O) external-tensor O(3bd O) has relative generic stable rank9abd²−1−epsilon(ad). Here epsilon(n) is one for even n and zero for odd n. This closes the residual thin strip, including4 dividing a withb=d=1.

The proof uses the ordinary Frobenius decomposition F_*O=O direct-sum B and two exact evaluation isomorphisms. A two-dimensional kernel-to-cokernel test is a residue matrix [[t,u],[v,t]]. Varying b1 by b1+lambda b2 fixes t and v and changes u by a polynomial with a nonzero linear coefficient. Separate evaluation arguments ensure both that coefficient and v are nonzero. The complete symbolic verification contains13 identities; it does not replace the all-degree proof.

The new positive-index nonproduct result is separate. For a mixed abelian surface with ordinary polarization index a>0, D=chi(M), and L=M³, the odd-degree ranks lie between9Dd²−2^a and9Dd²−2; the even-degree ranks lie between9Dd²−2^(a+1) and9Dd²−2. The a=1 odd-degree formula is exact. The upper bound is a scheme-theoretic Prym obstruction, and the lower bounds descend the actual line bundle through the entire ordinary etale kernel and pull back an index-zero sharp curve. The connected etale pullback multiplies the defect exactly. Sharpness for a>=2 in odd degree and every positive a in even degree remains open. No index-zero ample class on the original surface is assumed.

## Every degree at transcendental ordinary modulus

For X=E_o times E_s with the (3,3) embedding, when j(E_o) is transcendental over F2, the odd-degree geometric and arithmetic groups are GL_(9d²−1)(F2). The even-degree groups are the full pointwise stabilizer of two independent covectors, Hom(F2²,F2^(9d²−4)) semidirect GL_(9d²−4)(F2), in rank9d²−2. Every nonzero invariant subspace contains the irreducible common covector kernel.

The proof treats the geometric generic ordinary modulus. A connected special frame fibre forces a connected geometric generic frame fibre by a normal finite-etale cover argument, requiring no properness of the coefficient open. In even degree two, two exact coefficient points lie in the total arithmetic family image; the geometric generic image is normal there. An actual GL8 block and a degree32 irreducible nonreciprocal Frobenius polynomial give GL32, while the second point excludes every incomplete translation kernel. Normality then yields the whole geometric generic stabilizer. Explicit normalized derivations over F2(t) establish the two arithmetic covectors without a perfect-base shortcut. Every even degree at least four follows from the mixed intersection-Hasse degree argument.

This does not prove the groups for each fixed algebraic ordinary j, including finite-field elliptic curves. Reversing specialization would be invalid. The candidate file was renamed to generic_mixed_product_all_groups.tex upon promotion; its six existing mathematical identifiers retain their suffixes for identity continuity, with visible status Proved. Its final scope remark has the explicit identifier rem:generic-mixed-modulus-gate.

## The sharp unramified dyadic height-two index

The exact least manuscript index is now nu_min(2,1,2)=3, using M(nu)=ker2^(nu+1). Thus16-torsion determines the prime-to-two inertia character in the stipulated potentially good height-two class, and the earlier explicit8-torsion ambiguity makes this sharp. Within the potentially supersingular elliptic subclass,8-torsion already suffices.

The proof first realizes every finite height-two supersingular inertial type by an actual elliptic deformation and excludes mixed height-one/height-two comparisons at16. A graph/logarithm bound narrows the joint good-reduction degrees. The residual images1,C2,C3 are then treated exhaustively. Full rational2-torsion uses explicit Legendre/Kummer matrices; residualC2 passes to the unique rational2-isogeny quotient and compares quadratic-field valuations. ResidualC3 uses the actual marked8-congruence models, with their four Weil-pairing multipliers, and a trace-zero cubic normalization. The source family's universal discriminant identity and all valuation branches are checked exactly. The marked-family exhaustion is justified over every characteristic-zero field, including j=0 and1728, by Chen's finite-group cocycles and Fisher's Hesse family. The corresponding p3,e2,height2 index remains the previously proved value2. Other heights and ramification indices remain open.
