## Checkpoint 17 work: generic nonordinary surfaces and uniform mixed degree one

The work remains **INCOMPLETE** under the item-by-item requirements. The original scans remain unavailable; manuscript quotations are taken from the supplied AI transcriptions and their stated uncertainties. The work is AI-produced by **GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode)**, with no claim of priority. No remark from Michel Hua's project is used.

### Proved advances

1. **Every fixed mixed product in degree one.** For an ordinary elliptic curve and a supersingular elliptic curve over any perfect field of characteristic two, the complete (3,3) system has relative rank eight and geometric and arithmetic image GL8(F2). This includes all algebraic ordinary moduli. The universal relative determinant is D²Q, where D is the 3-by-3 determinant and Q is a smooth Frobenius cubic. A moving-kernel argument over the strictly henselian generic point of Q retains its imperfect residue field and gives seven independent Artin–Schreier inertia directions. The exceptional part of the nonzero-vector Lang incidence has dimension at most eight: its rank-two case is controlled by a smooth Frobenius Gram map, and its rank-one cases by the smooth elliptic determinant pencil and an additional cubic. The main incidence is an irreducible affine-line family of dimension nine. Thus the 255 nonzero vectors form one orbit. Conjugating the full root subgroup supplies elementary matrices and proves GL8 without a finite-group classification. All six mathematical assertions and the scope remark received full independent root and companion audits. Higher degrees at a fixed algebraic ordinary modulus remain open.

2. **All nonordinary ppav geometric generic moduli, in every degree.** On the p-rank-one stratum and on each p-rank-zero component of principally polarized abelian surfaces in characteristic two, every geometric generic modulus has odd-degree group GL_(9d²−1)(F2). In even degree the image is the full stabilizer of its f+1 invariant covectors, namely Hom(F2^(f+1),F2^(9d²−4)) semidirect GL_(9d²−4), acting on relative rank 9d²−3+f. The arithmetic image is the same over a perfect field of definition. Every finite prescribed set of degrees has a nonempty open of that stratum/component and actual finite-field examples. The proof does not assert that a single finite-field point lies in an intersection over all degrees. It uses a reduced-base constant-rank construction, a normal-base frame-component inequality, and the actual superspecial point on the normalization of each supersingular component. The fixed subgroup bound is explicitly required when converting group-order equality into group equality.

3. **An exact positive-index rank deformation gate.** The toral lattice I=ann(s,es) on a mixed surface has rank b−2, determinant O(−b), no global sections, and contains the full coherent Frobenius image. Sharpness is equivalent to nonvanishing of its degree-b determinant. At an étale double pullback of a sharp positive-index source, its restricted first Frobenius image is already stable of rank b−4, with two-dimensional kernel and cokernel. The first variation vanishes on pullback directions and factors through the trace quotient of sections. This reduces the remaining sufficient test to a quadratic determinant of a linear map into 2-by-2 matrices. General nonvanishing is not proved. The full coherent first rank is deliberately distinguished from the restricted first/stable rank; exact examples give different full first ranks. An attempted further factorization through the source Cartier cokernel failed and its program/output are retained.

4. **Tame height two at minimal cyclotomic ramification.** For every p≥5, e=p−1 and height two, 1≤nu_min≤2 in the manuscript convention M(nu)=ker p^(nu+1). Thus p³-torsion determines the requested prime-to-p inertia character. A formal height-two group over a DVR with absolute ramification a≤(p−1)(p²−1), p not dividing a, has no rational point of exact order p²: its p-typical valuation equations would force a=p(b+(p−1)A). Quotienting and twisting a hypothetical mixed comparison converts it to precisely such a point. Every remaining p² ambiguity is between two whole potentially supersingular groups, with equal finite determinant characters and joint tame faithful degree m dividing p²−1 but m>p. No existence or exact least-index value within the interval is asserted. Finite reduced norms are retained; arbitrary formal groups are not replaced by elliptic curves.

The complete system |9Θ| on every fixed principally polarized abelian surface

The proof has several independently checked inputs. A nonordinary genus-two
curve cannot have a degree-three map with three distinct totally ramified

reduces two further total fibres to a separable quadratic remainder, and its

the cyclic and S3 possibilities and computes a bijective Cartier operator in
both. Each has a universal polynomial certificate, independently rerun with
the original outputs preserved. The no-triple statement requires no isotropy
of a subgroup killed by three.

For such a subgroup, tangent identifications on the theta curve are excluded
by its canonical map and the two geometric two-torsion cases. Consequently
every individual theta norm is integral nodal, with exactly two nodes per
unordered nonzero type. A nonproduct polarized (3,3)-neighbour exists for
every nonproduct nonordinary target: in rank zero, Cartier excludes every
product quotient; in rank one, uniqueness of each elliptic type and the
principal-degree-one retraction argument show that at most one maximal
isotropic subgroup can give a product quotient.

The three eigensystems for a nonzero three-torsion translation descend to
ample (1,3) line bundles. A complete fixed-divisor argument excludes a base
curve, and the nine-point theta-kernel orbit contradicts the intersection
number six if a base point remains. Their morphisms are finite. The chord
incidence then gives two-transitivity of each eighteen-node cover. The theta
difference cover is quadratic in characteristic two; its reduced branch
support has class 2Θ and no nonzero odd translation stabilizer. Its isolated
shifted branches give transpositions in each node type separately, hence the
full product of four S18 factors.

The gluing proof retains the source boundary's stable-rank drop. A generic
splitting modulo the translation kernel is a section of a finite etale
Artin--Schreier torsor over a normal Lang scheme. It extends over every
component by finite birational normality. At each selected pair collision,
constant component torsors have common strict-henselian local trivializations,
so the inertia image is exactly the corresponding graph line, including in
the inseparable-residue case. The source graph relation produces a target
vertex-star vector with eight ones and ten zeroes in each type. The full node
permutation group then forces every type heart into the translation kernel.
The independently proved clopen-closure graph criterion gives irreducibility
and the full linear group.

## A.3: the primitive polarization reduction

For a mixed abelian surface, let a and b be the integral ordinary and
local-local polarization indices of an ample line bundle M. Over algebraic
closure it has an actual maximal root H^(2^r)=M, r=min(a,b), with indices
a-r,b-r. The proof uses the complete finite group scheme A[2^r], the fppf
quotient, torsionfreeness of Hom, and the full characteristic-two symmetric
homomorphism/line-bundle descent in AV Proposition 11.2 and Corollary 11.3.
Divisibility in Pic0 corrects the result to an actual line-bundle identity.

When 0<a<=b, this identifies |M^(3d)| with an even exponent in the previously
proved ordinary-index-zero case. The relative stable rank is therefore
9χ(M)d²-2 in every positive degree. Together with the a=0 theorem, this
strictly reduces the remaining mixed nonproduct case to primitive a>0,b=0.
The a=1 odd-degree sector was already exact. The actual root need not descend
to the original field; the conclusion concerns geometric generic rank.

The further restricted Petri statement is an exact equivalent test. It uses
the symmetric cup-wedge map on H1(Q-dual), restricted to the actual determinant
direction space. Its common radical vanishes exactly when an invertible
trace-zero variation exists. The annihilator is H1(KP)-dual, with the twist P
essential. No lower bound for that restricted map is asserted. In particular,

## A.4: adding two odd degrees on every fixed nonordinary principal surface

Let A be a fixed principally polarized surface in characteristic two, of
two-rank f=0 or1. If its odd degrees a,b have the proved full linear images,
then its even degree d=a+b has geometric and arithmetic monodromy

    Hom(F2^(1+f), F2^(9d²-4)) semidirect GL_(9d²-4)(F2),

on the relative unit local system of rank9d²-3+f. The common kernel of the
1+f invariant covectors is irreducible and lies in every nonzero invariant
subspace. Combining this with the independently proved powers-of-three
induction gives every degree d=3^i+3^j, including2,4,6,10,12 and18, on every
fixed nonordinary surface. There is no generic-modulus restriction.

The proof checks the changes from degree two explicitly. Curve-jet strata
remain valid after multiplying three-theta sections by sections of a
globally generated factor nonzero at the specified points. Restriction
maps may have larger kernels, but their fibres remain affine and integral.
Both component systems provide actual independent linear blocks. Lifted
node covers give the full sum-zero wreath groups, and uniform Goursat and
natural-module H1 arguments supply all gluing columns, including ambient
columns. The common many-theta boundary uses two independent graph
projections, not a false identification of full stable fibres across a
rank drop. Exact normal Lang closure carries the needed splittings and
projections. Transvections then recover the full stabilizer group.

The uniform group separation is proved, rather than extrapolated from
orders of small finite groups. If r>=8, no symmetric group's composition
factors contain GL_r(F2): either a suitable even permutation has larger
two-power order than GL_r, or the two-part of the alternating group order
is strictly too small. The proof covers every node count.
